thread.title: Apple HomePod Grabs Small Share Of Smart Speaker Market

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple HomePod Grabs Small Share Of Smart Speaker Market
text:
Apple ( AAPL ) sold 3 million HomePod smart speakers in the U.S. in the product's first five months of availability, a research firm estimated Thursday. That gives it 6% of the total installed base of 50 million smart speakers as of June 30, Consumer Intelligence Research Partners said.
X The CIRP report puts Apple in third place in smart speakers behind Amazon ( AMZN ) and Alphabet 's ( GOOGL ) Google. Amazon Echo speakers lead the category, with 70% market share in the U.S. Google Home is second with 24% share, CIRP said.
"Apple introduced HomePod in the first quarter, and now has a small but meaningful share," Josh Lowitz, CIRP partner and co-founder, said in a news release. "It took a small share of the market from both Amazon and Google."
He noted that Amazon has a two-year head start in the market and both Amazon and Google offer lower-priced devices.

The Apple HomePod costs $349. The standard Google Home unit costs $129, but it also offers a smaller version for $49 and a large version for $399. The standard Amazon Echo speaker costs $99.99, with other models ranging from $49.99 to $229.99.
Apple started selling the HomePod on Feb. 9 in the U.S., U.K. and Australia. It billed the device as a premium music speaker with voice controls. The HomePod is designed as a home gadget that works best with the Apple Music subscription service. It also can act as a home assistant using Siri technology to answer spoken questions and simple commands.
Apple expanded distribution of HomePod to Canada, France and Germany starting June 18 .
